hints.title: Falling Triplet Step Minimization Obstacle
hints.text: Falling down an n x n matrix allows moving directly below or one column diagonally left or right. How can computing the minimum falling path ending at each cell from row to row find the global minimum path sum?

hints.title: Triplet Lower Arrival Invariant
hints.text: The minimum path sum to reach cell (r, c) is matrix[r][c] plus the minimum among the valid upper neighbors (r - 1, c - 1), (r - 1, c), and (r - 1, c + 1).

hints.title: 1D Row Triplet Compression Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a 1D array with the first row. For each subsequent row, update each column c by adding the cell value to the minimum of the previous row values at c - 1 (if c > 0), c, and c + 1 (if c < n - 1). Return the minimum element in the final array.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Processes all N^2 cells with constant 3-way comparisons per cell.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching without state storage explores 3^N paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Compresses 2D table into two 1D rows of size N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Boundary checking on left and right diagonal columns.
